shortDescription: create, update, or destroy Automation Platform Controller credential.

options.name: controller_config_file
options.description: Path to the controller config file. If provided, the other locations for config files will not be considered.

options.name: controller_host
options.description: URL to your Automation Platform Controller instance. If value not set, will try environment variable C(CONTROLLER_HOST) and then config files If value not specified by any means, the value of C(127.0.0.1) will be used

options.name: controller_oauthtoken
options.description: The OAuth token to use. This value can be in one of two formats. A string which is the token itself. (i.e. bqV5txm97wqJqtkxlMkhQz0pKhRMMX) A dictionary structure as returned by the token module. If value not set, will try environment variable C(CONTROLLER_OAUTH_TOKEN) and then config files

options.name: controller_password
options.description: Password for your controller instance. If value not set, will try environment variable C(CONTROLLER_PASSWORD) and then config files

options.name: controller_username
options.description: Username for your controller instance. If value not set, will try environment variable C(CONTROLLER_USERNAME) and then config files

options.name: copy_from
options.description: Name or id to copy the credential from. This will copy an existing credential and change any parameters supplied. The new credential name will be the one provided in the name parameter. The organization parameter is not used in this, to facilitate copy from one organization to another. Provide the id or use the lookup plugin to provide the id if multiple credentials share the same name.

options.name: credential_type
options.description: The credential type being created. Can be a built-in credential type such as "Machine", or a custom credential type such as "My Credential Type" Choices include Amazon Web Services, Ansible Galaxy/Automation Hub API Token, Centrify Vault Credential Provider Lookup, Container Registry, CyberArk Central Credential Provider Lookup, CyberArk Conjur Secret Lookup, Google Compute Engine, GitHub Personal Access Token, GitLab Personal Access Token, GPG Public Key, HashiCorp Vault Secret Lookup, HashiCor

options.name: description
options.description: The description to use for the credential.

options.name: inputs
options.description: Credential inputs where the keys are var names used in templating. Refer to the Automation Platform Controller documentation for example syntax. authorize (use this for net type) authorize_password (password for net credentials that require authorize) client (client or application ID for azure_rm type) security_token (STS token for aws type) secret (secret token for azure_rm type) tenant (tenant ID for azure_rm type) subscription (subscription ID for azure_rm type) domain (domain for openstack t

options.name: name
options.description: The name to use for the credential.

options.name: new_name
options.description: Setting this option will change the existing name (looked up via the name field.

options.name: organization
options.description: Organization name, ID, or named URL that should own the credential. This parameter is mutually exclusive with C(team) and C(user).

options.name: request_timeout
options.description: Specify the timeout Ansible should use in requests to the controller host. Defaults to 10s, but this is handled by the shared module_utils code

options.name: state
options.description: Desired state of the resource. C(exists) will not modify the resource if it is present.

options.name: team
options.description: Team name, ID, or named URL that should own this credential. This parameter is mutually exclusive with C(organization) and C(user).

options.name: update_secrets
options.description: C(true) will always update encrypted values. C(false) will only update encrypted values if a change is absolutely known to be needed.

options.name: user
options.description: User name, ID, or named URL that should own this credential. This parameter is mutually exclusive with C(organization) and C(team).

options.name: validate_certs
options.description: Whether to allow insecure connections to AWX. If C(no), SSL certificates will not be validated. This should only be used on personally controlled sites using self-signed certificates. If value not set, will try environment variable C(CONTROLLER_VERIFY_SSL) and then config files
